clues: This city grew in a wide river valley, near where two rivers join. Old canals drew river water out to farm fields in the dry land.
Night brings little relief from the heat in this city. Roads and walls soak up the sun all day, then let the heat out after dark.
In 1889, the capital of the land moved to this town. It kept that job in 1912, when the land became a state.
Summer heat here beats that of any other big city in the land. Its average summer highs are the hottest of all of them.
The laws of Arizona are made in this city. More folk live here than in any other state capital.
